A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same self-distillation study. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: Appendix B and Figure 7 report original Gaussian-mixture simulations, including 20 trials per error point and empirical weight and pre-activation distributions.

after.justification: v3 retains the Gaussian simulations in Appendix D and adds original CIFAR-10 classification experiments and sample-level analyses in Section 8 and Appendix H.

M1.justification: The losses, regularization, temperature-controlled pseudo-labeling, repeated distillation, early stopping, and bias-fixing procedures are retained. The ResNet experiments apply the existing logistic SD procedure to frozen image features.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates Gaussian-mixture classification only. v3 adds CIFAR-10 cat-versus-dog classification using ImageNet-pretrained ResNet features, with noisy and noiseless supervision. This substantially extends evaluation into a real-image domain while retaining the synthetic coverage.

E2.justification: The existing comparisons against optimal 0-SD, hard-label SD, noiseless training, and heuristic variants are retained. CIFAR-10 extends the existing 0-SD versus soft-label and hard-label 1-SD comparison; ResNet-18 and ResNet-50 are feature configurations, not additional competing methods.

E3.justification: The new empirical protocol uses 512- or 2048-dimensional frozen embeddings, sampled training subsets, corrupted training labels, clean test labels, and Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization minimizing test error (Appendix G). This supplements the retained Gaussian experiments and theoretical Nelder-Mead optimization rather than replacing their settings.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds a noiseless CIFAR-10 control testing the denoising explanation and a case study comparing base-model predictions, optimal teacher pseudo-labels, and student predictions. Existing Gaussian soft-versus-hard-label, stage-dynamics, and bias-fixing analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 defines Figure 7's previously unspecified error bars as standard errors over the already reported 20 trials. New CIFAR-10 Figures 5 and 9 report standard errors over 10 trials per point; this does not establish an increase in runs for existing experiments.

E6.justification: Figures 5, 9, and 10 add CIFAR-10 error curves and per-image predictions: noisy-data gains are more pronounced with ResNet-18, smaller with ResNet-50, and negligible without label noise. The plotted signal and uncertainty magnitudes also differ between v1 Figure 5B and v3 Figure 3B despite matching caption settings; their qualitative early-stopping trend remains.

T1.justification: v3 corrects inconsistent N/M-to-alpha asymptotic statements to M/N-to-alpha and explicitly allows zero moment exponents in Appendix C.2. It removes v1's non-Gaussian-noise extension footnote. The principal replica equations, full phase-transition theorem, and proofs are retained, with substantial relocation rather than new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and new fifth contribution explicitly claim qualitative confirmation of theoretical predictions on CIFAR-10 with ResNet features, extending the claimed empirical reach beyond the toy model. The central denoising, dataset-size, early-stopping, and bias-fixing claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of student-oriented, more confident teacher labels and explicit limitations concerning finite samples and transfer beyond CIFAR-10. It also explains majority-class collapse under excessive rescaled bias and corrects the infinite-regularization interpretation from ignoring features to averaging label-weighted features.

D1.justification: Appendix G adds a substantial reproducibility description covering preprocessing, embedding extraction, noise injection, sampling, Bayesian tuning, and AMD EPYC 9654 hardware with 512 GB memory and approximately two-hour runs. The anonymous notebook link is replaced by a named GitHub repository link.

R1.justification: v3 adds Takahashi's under-bagging work, CIFAR-10 and TorchVision references, and future-work connections to domain adaptation, curriculum learning, meta-learning, and feature learning. Derrida's self-averaging citation is removed. The central positioning against existing distillation analyses remains; publication-metadata updates do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the introduction, setup, theoretical explanation, results discussion, and conclusion are rewritten. The full statistical characterization moves into Appendix C, hyperparameter optimization into Appendix E, and future-work discussion into Appendix I. A notation appendix and conference checklist further reorganize the document.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. The schematic is redrawn and relocated; v1 Figure 4 and Figure 5B-C are combined into v3 Figure 3, while the phase diagram moves to Figure 8. New CIFAR-10 Figures 5, 9, and 10 and an appendix notation table substantially expand the displays.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the retained theory easier to follow and adds useful CIFAR-10 controls, clearer uncertainty reporting, and implementation details. The gain is limited: the new experiments concern single-stage classification on frozen features, and Appendix G.5 selects hyperparameters using test error, limiting their strength as independent generalization validation. The principal scientific conclusions remain stable.
